rationale: The previous design showed early off-track failures on both the oval and s-bend tracks, with low progress and multiple line loss events. The telemetry indicates the robot struggles to maintain stable control and recover from line loss effectively. To improve stability and responsiveness, I increased the base speed from 0.12 to 0.14 to encourage more forward progress, expecting the controller to handle the speed. I increased the proportional gain kp from 0.9 to 1.0 to strengthen the steering response to line position errors, while reducing the integral gain ki from 0.15 to 0.1 to lessen potential overshoot and oscillations. The derivative gain kd is slightly reduced from 0.05 to 0.04 to smooth control without excessive damping. Sensor weights remain the same as they correctly assign negative values to left sensors and positive to right sensors, supporting proper steering. The geometry remains unchanged as it was balanced and appropriate. The line loss strategy remains 'search_left' as it is reasonable for recovery. I expect these changes to increase progress and reduce line loss events by improving control responsiveness and stability. The requested measurements will confirm if the robot completes more of the track with lower RMS error, fewer line loss events, and controlled steering oscillation.
